# Purpose

A production model can put the process residual in three different places.
The same biomass and catch series then imply three different residual time
series, and a diagnostic that assumes the wrong place will call a coherent
stock misspecified. `pe()` calculates each placement from an `FLStock` and an
equilibrium object.

# The three updates

Catch \(C_y\) replaces \(F_y B_y\). Surplus production is \(SP_y\).

| `location` | Update | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"after"` | \(B_{y+1} = (B_y + SP_y - C_y)\, e^{\eta_y}\) | \(e^{\eta_y} = B_{y+1} / (B_y + SP_y - C_y)\) |
| `"before"` | \(B_{y+1} = (B_y + SP_y)\, e^{\eta_y} - C_y\) | \(e^{\eta_y} = (B_{y+1} + C_y) / (B_y + SP_y)\) |
| `"productivity"` | \(B_{y+1} = B_y + SP_y e^{\eta_y} - C_y\) | \(e^{\eta_y} = (B_{y+1} - B_y + C_y) / SP_y\) |

`scale = "log"` (the default) returns \(\eta_y\). `"mult"` returns
\(e^{\eta_y}\). `"relative"` returns \((B_{y+1} - B_y + C_y - SP_y) / B_y\)
for `"after"`, and \(e^{\eta_y} - 1\) otherwise.

# Where \(SP_y\) comes from

`production = "FLBRP"` reads equilibrium yield off the `FLBRP` at the observed
biomass. `production = "pellat"` uses the Pella–Tomlinson curve

$$
SP_y = (r/p)\, B_y \left(1 - (B_y/K)^p\right)
$$

with parameters from `pellatParams()` when `eq` is an `FLBRP`.

# Comparison

```{r pe-three, eval=FALSE}
library(FLCore)
library(FLBRP)
library(FLRebuild)

data(ple4)
eq <- brp(FLBRP(ple4))

after <- pe(ple4, eq, production = "pellat", location = "after")
before <- pe(ple4, eq, production = "pellat", location = "before")
onProd <- pe(ple4, eq, production = "pellat", location = "productivity")
```

Plot the three log-residual series on one panel before interpreting a run of
positive or negative residuals. A pattern that appears in only one placement
is an assumption about the timing of \(\eta\), not a property of the stock.

`plotPe()` draws the residual series for a fitted production model. `jabbaPE()`
and `spictPE()` are the same calculation specialised to those fits.
